ops.body:
yasyf-home layer 3 (source-read on-machine): **all three** manifests fail synckitd 0.36.2 strict decode (cc-pool: watch.backend; cookiesync: service.transport; reposync: watch.backend), and the new manifest model makes hand-writing impossible by design — ServiceSpec is now `{kind, socket, schema_fingerprint}` with the fingerprint validated against each consumer's code-computed value. Only consumer regeneration paths mint valid manifests, and those are the exact paths blocked per consumer (cc-pool: user-gated re-auth; reposync: state envelope, diagnosis pending; cookiesync: regen path unknown). `synckitd host add` parses manifests BEFORE state, so the state migration is wedged behind manifest decode — circular unless unregenerable manifests are ARCHIVED aside (never hand-migrated, never deleted).

Bigger thread: synckit commits `1dfff0f`/`b402ba4` hard-cut daemon/service ownership to **daemonkit** (matches cc-pool 0.64.8's caveat: "daemonkit owns the user LaunchAgent; Homebrew does not install a second daemon service"), and `434c652` (Jul 14) deleted the legacy-mesh migration tooling ("every host has long since converged" — yasyf-home hadn't). So the machine repair is a **cutover to daemonkit-owned services**, not a patch of the old model. Home lane now mapping the cutover path from source, report-only: the CLI verb that materializes the daemonkit-owned LaunchAgent, legacy-plist handling, cookiesync re-registration, empty-manifests-dir startup behavior, and host add's exact state writes/peer handling. Box lane armed with the archive-aside amendment (its manifests are same-era) and told to capture any ownership-registration output on restart instead of fighting it.

Home remains fully unrestarted and unmodified except one backup file (state.json.pre-v0.36.2-migration.bak); all manifest move-aside tests were restored with mtimes verified.
